prompt: IndexedDocument.java is provided and complete. Finish InvertedIndex.java so it maps every word to the sorted set of document ids containing it, and supports lookup plus a search that requires all of the given words.
explanation: An inverted index is a Map from word to a Set of document ids. Using a Set means a word repeated inside one document still records that id once, and a TreeSet keeps the ids sorted so lookup can return them directly. computeIfAbsent creates the set the first time a word is seen, and search intersects the id sets with retainAll, which leaves only the documents that contain every requested word.
hints: index.computeIfAbsent(word, key -> new TreeSet<>()).add(id) both creates the set on demand and records the id.
lookup must handle a missing word: index.get returns null, and you should return an empty list rather than that null.
For search, start from a mutable copy of the first word's results and call retainAll with each remaining word's results -- that is set intersection.
